objective: Recognise that a type alias may reference itself inside a property type to describe a recursive structure.
defects: keyed option carries a parenthetical explanation that gives it away
explanation does not say when self-reference is rejected

rewrite.explanation: The self-reference sits inside the element type of children, a position the compiler resolves lazily, so the alias compiles and describes a tree of any depth. A direct self-reference such as type T = T | number is rejected (TS2456: circularly references itself) because the checker has no base case. Nothing loops at runtime: types are erased and the declaration produces no JavaScript.
rewrite.hint: Look at where Tree appears on the right-hand side: directly, or inside an array element type? The compiler treats those two positions differently.

rationale: Verified in both directions (the recursive alias compiles, the direct circular alias does not); the give-away option label was the main defect.
